finding: Live reproduction of the ATM-GOV-0265 branch-commit-queue deadlock. A governed `atm git commit` whose pre-commit hook runs longer than the caller's timeout was killed (SIGTERM); it left its OWN branch-commit-queue lock (.atm/runtime/locks/git-commit-queue-refs-heads-main.lock) with ownerPid dead and headShaAtAcquire == current HEAD. Retrying failed with ATM_GIT_COMMIT_BRANCH_QUEUE_BUSY forever, because live self-heal only reclaims a stale lock when HEAD has moved (headMoved); a dead-pid, same-actor, same-HEAD lock is never reclaimed. The only remedy was owner-approved manual lock deletion, which dispatched agents are forbidden to perform.
expectedBehavior: Two mitigations: (1) The governed commit wrapper should install a SIGTERM/SIGINT cleanup handler that releases its own branch-commit-queue lock before exiting, so a timeout never orphans the queue. (2) Lock acquisition should reclaim a stale lock when the recorded ownerPid is confirmed dead AND actorId/sessionId match the requester, independent of headMoved — a dead process holding its own lock is never a real concurrent writer.
evidenceOrRepro: Task TASK-SKL-0029, actor claude-004-skl-0029-captain. First `atm git commit --auto-stage` hit a 2-minute timeout mid pre-commit-hook (exit 143). Orphan lock record.json: ownerPid 68528 (verified dead via ps), headShaAtAcquire 185a39d035c2a3d33d7fa72ad8793fbb9f697f5e == HEAD. Retry (even with --timeout-ms 540000) returned ATM_GIT_COMMIT_BRANCH_QUEUE_BUSY, headShaCurrent == headShaAtAcquire, retryable:true but permanently stuck. Recovered only via one-time owner-approved Remove-Item of the lock dir. Cross-ref ATM-GOV-0265.
followUp: Fold into ATM-GOV-0265: add dead-pid same-actor reclaim to the branch-commit-queue acquire path, and a graceful SIGTERM lock-release in the commit wrapper. Add tests: (a) dead ownerPid + same actor + unmoved HEAD is reclaimed; (b) SIGTERM during commit releases the lock. Also consider documenting/raising the default commit timeout since the hook legitimately exceeds 2 minutes.
